title: Early changes in CT-derived quantitative flow ratio after transcatheter aortic valve replacement: a serial coronary physiological assessment.
authors: Lieyou Li; Yonghui Yu; Xinjie Zeng; Lijun Luo; Zhongwei Shi; Linyan Chen; Feng Hu; Lin Fan
abstract:
Transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) is an established treatment for severe aortic valve stenosis, but its effects on coronary physiology remain incompletely understood. CT-derived quantitative flow ratio (CT-QFR) enables non-invasive assessment of coronary physiology. This study aimed to investigate the early changes in CT-QFR following TAVR.
This retrospective study included consecutive patients with severe aortic stenosis who underwent coronary computed tomography angiography before and within 7 days after TAVR. CT-QFR was calculated for all analyzable coronary vessels. Longitudinal changes in CT-QFR were evaluated using linear mixed-effects models with patient identifier as a random effect.
A total of 109 patients (324 coronary vessels) were analyzed. Plaque volume, plaque burden, and minimal lumen diameter remained unchanged after TAVR, whereas transvalvular pressure gradients decreased significantly. Overall, CT-QFR increased modestly following TAVR (β=0.018, P < 0.001). Significant increases were observed in the left anterior descending and right coronary arteries, whereas no significant change was detected in the left circumflex artery. Vessels with baseline %DS ≥50% demonstrated greater CT-QFR increases than those with less severe stenosis (interaction β=0.104, P < 0.001). Likewise, vessels with baseline CT-QFR <0.80 showed significantly larger post-TAVR increases than vessels with baseline CT-QFR ≥0.80 (interaction β=0.117, P < 0.001).
TAVR was associated with modest early increases in CT-QFR, particularly in vessels with greater anatomical stenosis or baseline physiological impairment. These findings suggest that coronary physiological assessment in severe aortic stenosis may be influenced by valve intervention and should be interpreted cautiously during the peri-TAVR period.

title: Temporal changes in dilated ascending aorta after transfemoral TAVR: a comparative analysis of bicuspid and tricuspid aortic valves.
authors: Qichen Xu; Zheng Xu; Xiaofu Dai; Liangwan Chen; Zhiqin Lin
abstract:
Transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) addresses valvular obstruction but leaves concomitant ascending aortic dilatation untreated. Whether bicuspid aortic valve (BAV) morphology inherently accelerates post-TAVR aortic expansion compared with tricuspid aortic valves (TAV) remains uncertain.
This retrospective cohort study included 189 older adults (BAV, n = 87; TAV, n = 102) with severe aortic stenosis and ascending aortic dilatation (≥4.5 cm) undergoing TAVR. Annualized aortic expansion rates were evaluated utilizing linear mixed-effects models derived from serial computed tomography angiography over a median 27.0-month follow-up.
No ascending aortic dissection, rupture, or elective aortic interventions occurred during follow-up. The adjusted annualized expansion rate at the mid-ascending aorta was low and comparable between the BAV and TAV cohorts (0.43 vs. 0.39 mm/year; interaction P = 0.364). Progression rates at the distal ascending aorta and sinuses of Valsalva similarly demonstrated no significant morphological differences. No patient exhibited rapid progression (>5 mm/year). Although moderate or greater paravalvular leakage occurred exclusively in BAV patients (4.8% vs. 0.0%; P = 0.043), its overall incidence was low (2.2%); however, the extremely small number of cases precluded a definitive statistical assessment of its impact on longitudinal aortic expansion.
In this selected cohort, dilated ascending aortas exhibited slow intermediate-term expansion following transfemoral TAVR utilizing self-expanding valves, with comparable rates between BAV and TAV morphologies. These findings suggest that conservative management of concomitant ascending aortic dilatation may be a reasonable strategy in older TAVR candidates during intermediate-term follow-up, provided that strict blood pressure control and rigorous imaging surveillance are maintained.

title: Mapping human genetic associations to drug targets in valvular heart disease: an integrative evidence synthesis.
authors: Sara Moura-Ferreira; Tuna Ustunkaya; Momina Siddiqui; Kishore Kukendrarajah; Floriaan Schmidt; Raheel Ahmed; Mohammed Khanji; Anwar Chahal; Jan Verwerft; Rui Providencia
abstract:
Valvular heart disease (VHD) lacks disease-modifying pharmacological therapies. Drug repurposing guided by human genetics may help identify therapeutic opportunities. We aimed to integrate human genetic associations, drug-target information, and clinical evidence to identify repurposing opportunities and prioritise potentially druggable targets across the VHD spectrum.
We retrieved VHD-associated genetic variants from the NHGRI-EBI Genome-Wide Association Studies Catalogue and Ensembl, interrogated annotated genes in the Open Targets Platform, and evaluated linked drugs through structured searches of MEDLINE and ClinicalTrials.gov. The study protocol was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251071741).
We identified 1464 genetic associations corresponding to 844 unique variants and 582 candidate genes. Of these genes, 431 had tractability information and 51 had linked compounds, comprising 388 distinct pharmacological agents, 273 in phase 3 or 4 of clinical development. Drug-linked targets were concentrated in aortic stenosis. Clinical evidence supported therapeutic potential for 14 drugs, with preclinical or mechanistic cardiovascular support for eight additional drugs and adverse cardiovascular signals for four. An exploratory evidence-weighted framework prioritised targets according to genetic-functional evidence, tissue and mechanistic context, and translational tractability.
This genetics-informed evidence synthesis identifies drug-repurposing opportunities and a substantial gap between genetically supported targets and available therapies. The findings provide a hypothesis-generating framework for mechanistic validation and future valve-focused studies.

title: Survival benefit in patients with native aortic regurgitation using a dedicated transcatherter valve vs non-dedicated transcatheter valves.
authors: Andrea Messori; Roberto Brunoro; Melania Rivano
journal: Cardiovascular revascularization medicine : including molecular interventions
abstract:
Until recently, no standard of care has been established for patients with symptomatic native aortic regurgitation (AR) who are unsuitable for surgery. Transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) has been explored in this setting using off-label, non-dedicated valves originally designed for aortic stenosis. The recent ALIGN-AR trial evaluated the Trilogy valve, a dedicated transcatheter device specifically designed for native AR.
We performed an indirect comparison between the overall survival (OS) reported for the Trilogy valve in ALIGN-AR and OS from seven single-arm studies using non-dedicated valves. Individual patient data were reconstructed from published Kaplan-Meier curves using the IPDfromKM method. To ensure homogeneity, the follow-up period for the survival analysis was truncated at 24 months. Survival was analyzed using both hazard ratios (HR) and restricted mean survival time (RMST).
The analysis included 492 patients treated with the Trilogy valve and 867 treated with non-dedicated valves. OS was significantly improved with the Trilogy valve (HR 0.399; 95% CI 0.275-0.578; p = 0.0000011). RMST at 12 months was 11.4 months for the Trilogy valve versus 10.4 months for non-dedicated valves, corresponding to an OS gain of 1.0 months (95% CI 0.72-1.32) over the first year.
In patients with native AR undergoing TAVI, use of the dedicated Trilogy valve was associated with a highly significant survival advantage compared with non-dedicated devices, corresponding to an approximate 1-month gain in OS during the first 12 months after implantation.

title: SGLT2 inhibitor therapy following aortic valve intervention for aortic stenosis: a systematic review and meta-analysis of mortality, heart failure, rhythm, renal, and valve-related outcomes.
authors: Hamzah Pratama Megantara; Iwan Dakota; Taofan Taofan; Suci Indrian; Ruth Grace Aurora; Suko Adiarto
abstract:
Residual mortality and heart-failure events remain common after aortic valve intervention for severe aortic stenosis. Sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) improve cardiovascular and renal outcomes in heart-failure, diabetes, and chronic kidney disease populations, but their role following transcatheter or surgical aortic valve intervention remains uncertain.
PubMed, Scopus, ScienceDirect, Cochrane Library, citation tracking, and manually identified eligible studies were screened through June 2026 for randomized and observational studies comparing SGLT2i with usual care or no SGLT2i after aortic valve intervention. The review was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251059332). Eligible populations included TAVR, SAVR, and bioprosthetic aortic valve evidence where available. Adjusted hazard ratios (HRs) were pooled using random-effects models while non-HR estimates and non-comparable endpoints were summarized narratively.
Twelve eligible reports were included, comprising one randomized trial and 11 observational studies. Most time-to-event estimates were reported from TAVR cohorts; two SAVR-only studies and one mixed bioprosthetic AVR study added complementary surgical and valve-durability data. In the pooled time-to-event analysis, SGLT2i use was associated with lower all-cause mortality (HR 0.69, 95% CI 0.60-0.79; I²=5%; p < 0.001). The study-defined composite clinical outcome was also lower (HR 0.68, 95% CI 0.53-0.89; I²=57%; p = 0.005), although component definitions differed across studies. Estimates for heart-failure hospitalization or exacerbation, atrial fibrillation, and acute kidney injury were not statistically significant.
SGLT2i use after aortic valve intervention was associated with lower all-cause mortality in pooled time-to-event analysis. SAVR data were clinically informative but were not sufficiently homogeneous for separate quantitative pooling. Findings for composite, heart-failure, rhythm, renal, and valve-related outcomes remain less certain. Dedicated randomized trials are needed to confirm whether the observed association reflects a treatment effect and to define patient selection, treatment timing, and peri-procedural safety.

title: Emergency Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation in Mixed Bicuspid Aortic Valve Disease With a Horizontal Aorta: Return of Spontaneous Circulation Only After Left Ventricular Unloading.
authors: Tommaso Simone; Greta Cattaneo; Luca Testa; Francesco Bedogni; Gaspare Cannone
abstract: A 74-year-old man with mixed bicuspid aortic valve disease, combining severe calcific stenosis with severe regurgitation, and a left ventricular ejection fraction of 26% presented in normotensive cardiogenic shock with anuria and an arterial lactate of 12 mmol/L. Computed tomography showed a fibrocalcific left-right raphe and an aortic angulation of 66 degrees. Emergency transfemoral transcatheter aortic valve implantation was undertaken. The delivery system could not be advanced across the aortic arch despite escalation of guidewire support, and ventricular fibrillation degenerated into pulseless electrical activity refractory to resuscitation. Peripheral venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation was established, after which a 29 mm self-expanding prosthesis was implanted with an acceptable haemodynamic result and patent coronary ostia. Pulseless electrical activity nonetheless persisted. Return of spontaneous circulation followed only after a microaxial pump was advanced retrogradely across the freshly deployed prosthesis under fluoroscopic guidance alone, establishing an ECMELLA configuration. The patient died of multiorgan failure two days later. This sequence identifies continued left ventricular loading, rather than any residual valve lesion, as the reason resuscitation failed, and argues for anticipating unloading when extracorporeal support is instituted across a valve just rendered competent in a severely dysfunctional ventricle. The outcome appeared determined by end-organ injury already established before intervention.

title: Association of Left Ventricular Outflow Tract Obstruction with Left Atrial Remodeling and Dysfunction in Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy: A Three-Dimensional Echocardiography and Left Atrial Strain Study.
authors: Weili Lin; Runming Zhong; Qianqian Que; Wenwen Lin; Rui'e Zhu; Fulai Cai
abstract:
To compare left atrial (LA) structure and phasic function among healthy controls and patients with nonobstructive or obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM), and assess their associations with left ventricular outflow tract obstruction (LVOTO).
We studied 90 patients with HCM and 50 healthy controls. Patients were classified by the highest resting or Valsalva-provoked LVOT gradient (LVOTG) as nonobstructive (<30 mmHg; n = 50) or obstructive (≥30 mmHg; n = 40). Threedimensional echocardiography measured LA volumes, and two-dimensional speckle tracking measured phasic strain. Multivariable linear regression examined prespecified echocardiographic outcomes by LVOTO status. Sensitivity analyses modeled LVOTG continuously and used a 50-mmHg threshold.
Both HCM groups had greater LA enlargement and dysfunction than controls, with the largest abnormalities in obstructive HCM. In the primary adjusted model, LVOTO was associated with higher LAVImin (B = 10.03 mL/m2; 95% CI, 6.71 to 13.36; p < 0.001) and lower LASr (B = -2.72%; 95% CI, -4.17 to -1.28; p < 0.001). The associations remained when LVOTG was analyzed per 10 mmHg and with a threshold of ≥50 mmHg. E/e' and TRV were not significantly associated with LVOTG in these sensitivity analyses.
In this cross-sectional HCM cohort, greater obstruction severity was associated with higher LAVImin and lower LASr. Prospective studies are needed to determine whether these measures are associated with clinical outcomes.

title: Coronary artery disease management in patients with severe aortic stenosis undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials.
authors: Kamil Bujak; Daniele Giacoppo; Claudio Laudani; Marco Spagnolo; Placido Maria Mazzone; Maria Sara Mauro; Luigi Cutore; Giacinto Di Leo; Simone Finocchiaro; Antonio Greco; Davide Capodanno
journal: EuroIntervention : journal of EuroPCR in collaboration with the Working Group on Interventional Cardiology of the European Society of Cardiology
abstract:
The optimal management of coronary artery disease in patients with severe aortic stenosis undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) remains uncertain.
We aimed to compare clinical outcomes between routine coronary revascularisation and conservative management in patients undergoing TAVI and to assess the relative effectiveness of individual revascularisation strategies by performing a meta-analysis of randomised trials.
We conducted a pairwise meta-analysis comparing percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) with conservative treatment and a network meta-analysis comparing the relative effectiveness of individual strategies, including angiography-guided and physiology-guided PCI. The primary outcome was a study-defined composite endpoint of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE). Secondary endpoints included the individual outcomes of all-cause death, cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction, stroke, unplanned revascularisation, and major bleeding.
Five trials (N=1,644 patients) were included in the systematic review, and four were included in the primary quantitative synthesis (N=1,476). Compared with conservative treatment, routine PCI was associated with lower risks of MACE (risk ratio [RR] 0.80, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.65-0.98) and unplanned revascularisation (RR 0.30, 95% CI: 0.11-0.83) and an increased risk of major bleeding (RR 1.57, 95% CI: 1.07-2.32). In the network meta-analysis, physiology-guided PCI significantly reduced MACE, stroke, and unplanned revascularisation compared with conservative treatment and ranked highest for all ischaemic outcomes among revascularisation strategies.
Among patients referred for TAVI, routine revascularisation reduces the risk of ischaemic outcomes compared with conservative treatment. In this setting, physiology-guided PCI may be associated with the most favourable efficacy profile across available strategies. (PROSPERO: CRD420261330194).

title: Extremely Severe Aortic Stenosis Mimicking Cardiac Amyloidosis on Multimodality Imaging.
authors: Yu Young Kim; Kyoungjune Pak; Ji Won Lee; Jung Hyun Choi
abstract:
Cardiac amyloidosis is increasingly recognized in older patients with severe aortic stenosis, yet advanced pressure-overload remodeling can produce overlapping imaging features that confound noninvasive diagnosis.
A 70-year-old woman presented with progressive exertional dyspnea and markedly elevated cardiac biomarkers. Transthoracic echocardiography revealed extremely severe calcific aortic stenosis, increased left ventricular wall thickness, and severely reduced global longitudinal strain. Cardiac magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated elevated native T1 and extracellular volume with late gadolinium enhancement, and cardiac amyloid radionuclide imaging showed Perugini grade 1 uptake. Despite clinical suspicion of cardiac amyloidosis, noninvasive findings remained inconclusive. The patient underwent surgical aortic valve replacement with intraoperative myocardial biopsy, which demonstrated cardiomyocyte hypertrophy and interstitial fibrosis without amyloid deposition, consistent with advanced pressure-overload remodeling rather than infiltrative disease.
Extremely severe aortic stenosis can mimic cardiac amyloidosis across multiple imaging modalities. Histologic confirmation remains essential when noninvasive findings are discordant or inconclusive.
Severe aortic stenosis may closely mimic cardiac amyloidosis on multimodality imaging. Histological confirmation can be decisive in resolving diagnostic uncertainty.

title: Clonal expansion of CD8+ effector T cells in patients with calcific aortic valve disease.
authors: Francesca Bartoli-Leonard; Sarvesh Chelvanambi; Tan Pham; Casandra L Clift; Mandy E Turner; Mark C Blaser; Sasha A Singh; Massimo Caputo; Masanori Aikawa; Amanda Pang; Jochen Muehlschlegel; Elena Aikawa
abstract:
Calcific aortic valve disease (CAVD) is a complex cardiovascular pathology, culminating in aortic stenosis and heart failure with no effective treatment strategy, except invasive surgery. While inflammation may contribute to valvular fibro-calcific pathology and T cells have been identified within the leaflets, their contribution to CAVD pathogenesis remains unclear.
Disease-staged whole-tissue proteomics (n=16) confirmed a pro-inflammatory T cell driven signature, with immunohistochemistry (n=10) and immunofluorescence (n=8) conducted on control and CAVD valves to confirm T cell localization to calcified regions. Flow cytometry immunophenotyping (n=20) was was performed using valvular tissue and corresponding peripheral blood from the same individuals. Single cell RNA sequencing and paired single T cell receptor sequencing was conducted on an additional 4 patients on CD45+, CD3+, CD4+ or CD8+ T cells. T cell signaling was identified through unsupervised clustering. Tissue resident memory (TRM) T cells were detected within the valve, exhibiting a highly cytotoxic, activated, and terminally differentiated phenotype. This pan-pro-inflammatory signal was differentially identified in T cells originating from the valve tissue, and not observed in the blood, indicative of an adaptive, local and non-systemic inflammatory signature in CAVD patients. T cell receptor analysis detected hyperexpanded clones within the CD8+ T cell central memory (TCM) population, with TRM cells comprising most of the large and medium clonal expansion within the T cell population. Clonal expansion was more prominent in valve tissue, with expanded clones largely confined to their tissue of origin. Clonal interaction network analysis demonstrated the greatest proportion of clones originating from CD8+ TCM and TRM populations, exhibiting a tissue resident, cytotoxic environment within the valve.
Taken together, the data define distinct T cell subpopulations in CAVD and implicate specific antigenic epitopes driving clonal expansion of valvular T cells, supporting a central role for antigen-driven, autoimmune-like inflammation in disease propagation.

title: Anatomical Variations of Renal Arteries: Clinical, Radiological, and Surgical Considerations.
authors: Evangelos Rodinos; Dimosthenis Chrysikos; Theodore Troupis
abstract:
To synthesize the current knowledge regarding the embryological basis, anatomical classification, imaging characterization, and clinical implications of accessory renal arteries.
Anatomical variations in the renal arteries are common, affecting approximately 20-35% of the population, and have significant implications for clinical outcomes and surgical planning. Accessory renal arteries are usually terminal vessels that serve discrete renal islands with minimal collateral circulation in the body; therefore, their preoperative identification is important. However, there has been no modern synthesis of embryology, imaging, and multidisciplinary clinical treatment for these variations.
A narrative review of the literature was conducted by searching PubMed and Google Scholar for publications from December 2015 to December 2025. MeSH terms and free-text keywords related to "accessory renal artery," "multiple renal arteries," "renal artery variations," "renal vascular anatomy," "kidney transplantation," "renovascular hypertension," "computed tomography angiography," "magnetic resonance angiography," and "endovascular aortic repair" were used in Boolean combinations. Peer-reviewed original studies, systematic reviews, meta-analyses, and case series were included. Conference abstracts, unpublished data, and non-English publications were excluded.
This review addresses the embryological basis and anatomical classification of accessory renal arteries; the diagnostic roles of Doppler ultrasound, computed tomography angiography, and magnetic resonance angiography; and their clinical implications in kidney transplantation, partial nephrectomy, and endovascular aortic repair, including the contested association with renovascular hypertension. Available data suggest that most accessory vessels do not independently cause hypertension, whereas stenosis of larger vessels may be a correctable etiology in selected cases.
Accessory renal arteries have a significant clinical impact, primarily determined by the size of the vessels and the area of the kidney they supply. Preoperative characterization based on modern imaging can be reliable and can help plan and manage surgery for each patient. More prospective research is required to establish evidence-based principles for vessel maintenance and evaluate new technologies in this context.

title: Late-Onset Prosthetic Valve Dysfunction Associated With Hypoattenuated Leaflet Thickening Detected After a New Heart Murmur: A Case Report.
authors: Kazuyoshi Takagi; Kosuke Saku; Hiroki Mine; Takanori Kono; Eiki Tayama
abstract: Hypoattenuated leaflet thickening (HALT) is increasingly recognized after bioprosthetic aortic valve replacement; however, its clinical significance and optimal detection strategy in routine practice remain uncertain. We report the case of a 79-year-old woman who underwent minimally invasive aortic valve replacement using a Perceval S sutureless bioprosthesis for severe aortic stenosis. Early postoperative transthoracic echocardiography and cardiac computed tomography demonstrated normal prosthetic valve function without evidence of HALT. Oral anticoagulation was discontinued three months after surgery, and the patient remained asymptomatic. At the one-year follow-up visit, a newly detected systolic heart murmur prompted further evaluation despite stable N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide levels. Echocardiography revealed increased transvalvular gradients and mild-to-moderate transvalvular regurgitation, while cardiac computed tomography demonstrated HALT involving the right and noncoronary cusps. The combination of hemodynamically significant prosthetic valve dysfunction and CT-confirmed HALT was considered consistent with clinically overt bioprosthetic valve thrombosis. Oral anticoagulation was restarted, followed by complete resolution of HALT and improvement in prosthetic valve hemodynamics. This case demonstrates that clinically overt bioprosthetic valve thrombosis associated with HALT may develop in an asymptomatic patient and that a newly detected cardiac murmur may serve as a clinical trigger for further echocardiographic and CT evaluation. Careful routine clinical follow-up may facilitate recognition of hemodynamically relevant prosthetic valve dysfunction and appropriate therapeutic intervention.

title: Early Post-transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation (TAVI) Haemodynamics With SAPIEN Balloon-Expandable and Evolut Self-Expanding Valve Platforms: A Retrospective Single-Centre Cohort Study.
authors: Behzad Masood; Mamoon Ahmed; Syed M Usman; Afzaal Aleem Khan; Saba Ayub
abstract: Introduction Balloon-expandable valves (BEVs) and self-expanding valves (SEVs) have different frame architectures, leaflet positions and distinct deployment mechanics that may influence prosthetic haemodynamics. We compared early echocardiographic gradients after transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) between SAPIEN BEV and Evolut SEV platforms in a routine-practice cohort spanning several device generations. Materials and methods We retrospectively analysed 665 TAVI procedures: 250 BEV procedures using SAPIEN 3 variants and 415 SEV procedures using Evolut variants. The primary endpoint was the early post-TAVI echocardiographic mean transvalvular gradient obtained within three months of TAVI. Secondary endpoints were absolute and relative gradient reductions, achievement of a post-TAVI mean gradient <10 mmHg, and a residual mean gradient ≥20 mmHg. Because the continuous variables were skewed, they were compared using two-sided Mann-Whitney U tests. Results were reported as medians with interquartile ranges, with bootstrap 95% confidence intervals (CIs) for differences in medians. Categorical variables were compared using Pearson chi-square tests without continuity correction when expected counts were adequate and Fisher's exact tests when cell counts were small. Paired pre- and post-TAVI measurements were compared using Wilcoxon signed-rank tests. Multivariable ordinary least-squares regression with HC3 heteroscedasticity-robust standard errors was used to adjust the post-TAVI gradient for the baseline gradient and available prespecified covariates. Results Complete pre- and post-TAVI gradients were available for 664 procedures (249 BEV and 415 SEV). The median post-TAVI gradient was 8.4 (5.85-11.63) mmHg with SEV and 10.0 (7.93-13.90) mmHg with BEV (median difference, -1.60 mmHg; bootstrap 95% CI: -2.97 to -1.00; Mann-Whitney U test: p < 0.001). The median absolute gradient reduction was also greater with SEVs (36.0 vs 32.0 mmHg; median difference, 4.0 mmHg; p < 0.001), as was the relative gradient reduction (81.52% vs 76.19%; median difference, 5.33 percentage points; p < 0.001), although SEVs had a higher pre-procedural baseline transvalvular gradient. A post-TAVI mean gradient <10 mmHg was recorded in 61.2% of SEV procedures compared with 43.4% of BEV procedures (risk ratio 1.41; p < 0.001). Residual gradients of ≥20 mmHg were uncommon and did not differ between the two groups (6.0% in SEV procedures vs 5.6% in BEV procedures; p = 0.831). After adjustment, in 575 completed cases, SEV use remained associated with a 1.48 mmHg lower post-TAVI mean gradient (95% CI: -2.42 to -0.55; p = 0.0019). Conclusions In this cohort, Evolut SEV procedures were associated with a modestly lower early post-TAVI mean gradient than SAPIEN BEV procedures. The magnitude of this association, and its interpretation alongside baseline gradient, anatomy, and other device-selection factors, can inform further comparative evaluation. No clinical outcomes or valve-durability measures were assessed.

title: Ultralow-contrast stepping digital subtraction angiography for whole-limb arterial evaluation: A case report.
authors: Mitsunari Maruyama; Yuki Kimura; Megumi Nakamura
abstract: Stepping digital subtraction angiography (DSA) enables whole-limb arterial assessment with a single contrast injection, and diluted contrast medium may further reduce iodine exposure. A patient in their 80s with an abdominal aortic aneurysm and bilateral common iliac artery aneurysms was scheduled for staged internal iliac artery embolization before endovascular aneurysm repair (EVAR). Due to a mural thrombus in the left common iliac artery aneurysm, right internal iliac artery embolization was performed via an ipsilateral approach. Severe right external iliac artery stenosis prompted stepping DSA before and after embolization to evaluate distal embolization. Sevenfold- and tenfold-diluted stepping DSA examinations were performed before and after embolization, respectively, using identical injection parameters (3 mL/s; 30 mL). These required 4.29 and 3.0 mL of undiluted contrast medium, respectively. Although pedal artery enhancement was reduced with tenfold dilution, image quality remained acceptable, and no obvious distal embolization was identified in the visualized arteries; however, small emboli in poorly opacified pedal branches could not be excluded with tenfold dilution. Because internal iliac artery embolization was not expected to significantly alter lower-extremity arterial perfusion, the observed difference in image quality was considered to primarily reflect the difference between the two dilution protocols rather than changes in arterial hemodynamics. Ultralow-contrast stepping DSA may be a contrast-saving technique in selected cases when repeated whole-limb arterial evaluation is required.

title: [Evidence-based treatment of valvular heart disease].
authors: Felix S Nettersheim; Stephan Baldus
abstract: Valvular heart disease is a major cause of cardiovascular morbidity and mortality worldwide. As the prevalence of most valvular heart diseases increases with age, population ageing has led to a substantial increase in disease burden. Due to advanced age or significant comorbidities, many patients are considered unsuitable for conventional surgery. Whereas medical therapy was therefore often the only treatment option in the past, the rapid evolution of transcatheter interventions has fundamentally transformed the management of valvular heart disease over the past two decades. Today, effective catheter-based treatment options are available for virtually all valvular pathologies. For patients with severe symptomatic aortic stenosis, the prognostic benefit of transcatheter aortic valve replacement is firmly established. Large randomized trials have demonstrated non-inferiority of transcatheter aortic valve replacement compared with surgical aortic valve replacement across most patient populations, leading to an expanding use of this approach in younger and lower-risk patients. Similarly, transcatheter edge-to-edge repair for mitral and tricuspid regurgitation has been shown to improve symptoms, quality of life, and heart failure-related hospitalizations. In carefully selected patients with secondary mitral regurgitation, this strategy also confers a survival benefit. In addition, dedicated transcatheter devices have recently emerged as promising treatment options for native aortic regurgitation. Given the rapid evolution of transcatheter therapies, current efforts are increasingly focused on selecting the optimal treatment strategy for the individual patient and determining the optimal timing of intervention.

title: Femoral-to-Carotid Shunting During Carotid-Access TAVR in Moyamoya-Pattern Vasculopathy.
authors: Nicolas Mourad; Albert W Chan; Keerit Tauh
abstract:
Carotid access is an alternative for transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) in patients with prohibitive transfemoral anatomy, but it may cause cerebral hypoperfusion with impaired intracranial collateral circulation.
A 67-year-old woman with symptomatic severe aortic stenosis, extensive comorbidities, and unsuitable transfemoral access underwent TAVR. Neuroimaging demonstrated moyamoya-pattern intracranial vasculopathy with limited collateral reserve. During left carotid exposure, test occlusion caused a >50% decline in cerebral near-infrared spectroscopy despite blood pressure augmentation. A femoral-to-carotid arterial shunt was established to maintain cerebral perfusion. A 26-mm self-expanding Evolut FX+ valve was successfully implanted via left carotid access, with excellent hemodynamics and no neurologic complications.
This approach demonstrates a novel cerebral protection strategy for selected patients with compromised cerebrovascular reserve.
Carotid-access TAVR in moyamoya-pattern vasculopathy carries hypoperfusion risk. Real-time near-infrared spectroscopy may detect intolerance to carotid clamping, while femoral-to-carotid shunting may offer cerebral protection.

title: Targeted molecular CT imaging of atherosclerosis and abdominal aortic aneurysm.
authors: Jannis Marchand; Felix Stefan Reuter; Hannah Lichtmannegger; Keno Kyrill Bressem; Lisa Christine Adams; Franz Pfeiffer; Avan Kader; Marcus Richard Makowski
abstract: Atherosclerosis and abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA) share the same pathological triad, which includes chronic inflammation, immune cell infiltration, and extracellular matrix (ECM) degradation. Both diseases are characterized by the fact that the disease process may not be diagnosed until a life-threatening event occurs. Current imaging methods diagnose these conditions by assessing the degree of stenosis of the blood vessel, the plaque burden, and the aneurysm diameter. Unfortunately, these methods are not sufficient to measure biological activity, which is important to determine if such potentially life-threatening events will occur and where they will occur. Molecular imaging, together with computed tomography (CT), might close this gap. CT offers several benefits: it is widely available, allows rapid acquisition, can be integrated into vascular workflows, and can provide quantitative signal readout, but its main use has been in the context of anatomical detail. Recent preclinical studies suggest that a shift may be occurring in this area. This review examines the use of molecular CT imaging for the diagnosis of atherosclerosis and AAA, systematically grouped by molecular target. There are three different approaches that are employed in the current literature. The most clinically advanced is the first, macrophage-targeted probes. The second, high-density lipoprotein (HDL)-mimetic nanoparticles, takes advantage of an endogenous lipoprotein pathway, but not an engineered ligand. The third, gold nanoparticles, which targeted elastin, yielded the most clinically relevant finding to date: ex vivo signal correlates inversely with aortic wall burst pressure, casting doubt on whether diameter is sufficient to assess for rupture. Comparable methods for targeting biomarkers with CT have not been developed, although magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) and nuclear imaging modalities can already target matrix metalloproteinase (MMP) activity, vascular cell adhesion molecule-1 (VCAM-1), and microcalcification. This is a space that could be very fruitful for future studies.

abstract: Introduction: Height, weight, and age of person has significant impact on the normal size of heart. title: Understanding pedagogical challenges faced by technology teachers in special needs classrooms
authors: Katane Elizabeth Kekana; Thokozani Isaac Mtshali
journal: Journal of Education and Learning Technology
abstract: Teaching learners with special educational needs requires dynamic and adaptive pedagogical strategies that can lead to social development and academic success. This can be possible if teachers are assisted in mitigating the daily challenges of teaching such learners. This qualitative exploratory case study investigated the pedagogical challenges encountered by two Grade 9 Technology teachers in the Capricorn District of Limpopo Province. This study used Shulman’s Content and Pedagogical Knowledge framework to understand teachers’ challenges. Data was collected through semi-structured interviews and classroom observations; all collected data were analysed thematically. This study found that teachers experienced various challenges, including the emotional labour of teaching, burnout in the LSEN environment and the enactment of instructional knowledge. The study concluded that the sampled teachers displayed weaknesses in lesson planning, activating learners’ prior knowledge, diagnosing errors, achieving curriculum objectives and sustaining engagement. As a result, it was recommended that support through teacher assistants, creative differentiated strategies and enhanced digital-technology literacy to improve outcomes for learners with special needs was imminent.

title: Integration of Biomechanics and Digital Technology: Using Kinovea for Motion Analysis and Learning for Beginner Athletes
authors: Muhammad Nur Hudha; Riezky Maya Probosari; Annisa Nur Khasanah; Supurwoko; Salsabila Kholifahtun Nisa’; Gifran Rihla Gifarka Latief
journal: Journal of Coaching and Sports Science
abstract: Background: The integration of biomechanics with digital motion-analysis technologies has introduced new approaches for examining movement efficiency, kinematic characteristics, and technical patterns in walking and running activities. Kinovea, as an accessible motion-analysis software, provides both visual and quantitative feedback. However, its application in supporting technique development among beginner athletes remains insufficiently explored. Aim: This study aims to describe the use of Kinovea in biomechanics training and examine its contribution to the awareness of kinematic characteristics and movement techniques among beginner athletes. Methods: A descriptive qualitative design involved 72 beginner athletes aged 18–25 years selected through purposive sampling. Data were collected over 16 weeks through interviews, field observations, and motion video recordings analyzed using Kinovea. Kinematic data focused on joint angles, stride behavior, and movement phases during walking, running, and the flight phase. Qualitative data were analyzed using content analysis with NVivo 12, while kinematic results were interpreted descriptively to identify performance patterns and areas for technical refinement. Result: Kinematic analysis showed coordinated joint-angle patterns across all phases. Walking analysis identified arm swing angles of 50.9°–58.8° and leg separation angles of 64.3°–67.2°, indicating a stable gait rhythm. The running analysis revealed knee angles of 68.8°–69.8° and elbow angles of 87.6°–89.1°, indicating efficient propulsive mechanics. The flight phase demonstrated knee angles of 81.2°–87.8° and elbow angles of 80.4°–88.3°, suggesting effective momentum use and postural stability. These measurements supported stride-efficiency assessment and technique evaluation. Qualitative findings revealed that Kinovea enabled athletes to interpret movement phases and identify technical inefficiencies through slow-motion and frame-by-frame visualization. Conclusion: Kinovea supports basic motion analysis by providing clear kinematic information and helping beginner athletes observe and refine their movement techniques. The findings also offer practical value for coaches by enabling more precise identification of inefficient patterns and guiding targeted corrections during early-stage training.

title: A Review of Phishing Detection Techniques Using Machine Learning and Natural Language Processing
authors: Dr. Sunita Dixit
journal: Journal of Global Research in Multidisciplinary Studies(JGRMS)
abstract: The goal of phishing attacks, which rank high among cyber risks, is to steal sensitive information (such as login passwords, financial data, and more) from unsuspecting people and companies. Blacklist, whitelist, rule, heuristic, and signature-based detection methods are no longer suitable due to the rising sophistication of phishing schemes. As a result, ML, DL, and NLP are rapidly becoming into effective instruments for detecting both well-known and brand-new forms of phishing. Background on phishing assaults, old ways of detecting them, and recent advances in intelligent phishing detection are all included in this article. It delves into several machine learning algorithms such as decision tree, LSTM, ANN, CNN, and RNN, as well as deep learning models like KNN, NB, and SVM. Also, natural language processing methods including word embedding, sentiment analysis, text categorization, and tokenization are explored with the aim of detecting phishing material. Presenting a comprehensive, precise, and up-to-the-minute phishing detection system is the ultimate goal of this study, which focuses on machine learning frameworks, performance indicators, present obstacles, and future research directions.

journal: Научный журнал "Вестник Актюбинского регионального университета имени К. Жубанова"
abstract: In the context of increasing complexity of modern network infrastructures and the growing number of cyberattacks, improving the effectiveness of intrusion detection systems is a highly relevant task. The aim of this work is to develop and investigate a hybrid approach to network attack detection based on a combination of signature-based analysis and intelligent machine learning methods.  The research methods include analysis of requirements for anomaly detection systems, comparative analysis of existing solutions, design of a hybrid system architecture, and experimental modeling using multiclass classification of network traffic. The results demonstrate that integrating a neural model with a traditional detection system improves attack detection coverage and reduces the number of false positives.  The practical significance of the study lies in the possibility of deploying the proposed architecture in real corporate networks, while the theoretical significance consists in substantiating the effectiveness of a hybrid approach to traffic analysis. Future research directions include adaptive model training and expansion of the range of detectable attacks.

title: Neuronal intermediate filament neurologic autoimmunity in a patient with Merkel cell carcinoma receiving pembrolizumab
authors: Ali Hijazi; Saffet Guleryuz; Mark Andrew Walshauser; Ghazala R. Hayat; Maithreyi Chappidi
abstract: Abstract Background Neuronal intermediate filament (NIF) autoimmunity is an uncommon paraneoplastic neurologic syndrome that has increasingly been recognized in association with immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) therapy. Merkel cell carcinoma is among the malignancies most frequently associated with NIF antibodies, although reported cases remain limited. Case Presentation A 55-year-old female with stage IIIA Merkel cell carcinoma developed vertigo, gait instability, dysarthria, and persistent right hemifacial and cervical spasms after receiving second dose of pembrolizumab for recurrent disease. Brain MRI was unremarkable, while continuous electroencephalography demonstrated encephalopathy without a definitive electrocerebral correlate, raising suspicion for subcortical myoclonus. Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) analysis revealed lymphocytic pleocytosis, elevated protein. CSF and positive NIF antibodies using cell-based assay. Pembrolizumab was discontinued, and the patient was treated with high-dose corticosteroids followed by monthly intravenous immunoglobulin, resulting in near complete resolution of her neurologic symptoms after 6 months. Conclusion This case expands the growing spectrum of ICI-associated NIF paraneoplastic neurologic autoimmunity complicating Merkel cell carcinoma. To our knowledge, persistent hemifacial and cervical spasm has rarely been reported in this clinical setting. Early recognition of this syndrome, prompt antibody testing, discontinuation of ICI therapy, and initiation of therapy may improve neurological outcomes while informing further oncologic management.

title: Reproducibility dataset for: Experimental validation of spectral redistribution theory in intracranial aneurysm and aortic valve flow
authors: Khalid M. Saqr
journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: This research object contains the data products, analysis code, provenance records, quality control outputs, figure source data, and final figures supporting the study “Experimental validation of spectral redistribution theory in intracranial aneurysm and aortic valve flow.” The study extends the theoretical framework introduced by Khalid M. Saqr in “Resonant spectral cascade in Womersley flow triggered by arterial geometry,” Physics of Fluids 38, 041901, 2026, DOI 10.1063/5.0319995. That work predicted that geometric modulation of pulsatile arterial flow can redistribute wave energy across axial spatial scales. A central prediction of the theory is that increased relative energy at higher axial wavenumbers can occur while the total wave energy is decreasing. The present experimental analysis examines that prediction directly in measured spatial velocity fields. Two independent experimental datasets provide the basis of the study. The intracranial aneurysm analysis uses the experimental measurements reported by Brindise and colleagues in “Multi modality cerebral aneurysm haemodynamic analysis in vivo 4D flow MRI, in vitro volumetric particle velocimetry and in silico computational fluid dynamics,” Journal of the Royal Society Interface, DOI 10.1098/rsif.2019.0465. The corresponding public dataset is hosted by the Purdue University Research Repository under the record “In vitro Volumetric Particle Velocimetry, Computational Fluid Dynamics CFD, and in vivo 4D Flow MRI Hemodynamic Data in Two Patient Specific Cerebral Aneurysms.” The present work uses the volumetric particle tracking measurements from the ANY007 model. These measurements permit direct evaluation of axial spectral structure across the global field and within anatomically defined regions including the parent artery, aneurysm neck, core, and dome. The aortic valve analysis uses the measurements reported by Till Zeugin and colleagues in “In vitro investigation of the blood flow downstream of a 3D printed aortic valve,” Scientific Reports, DOI 10.1038/s41598-024-51676-6. The corresponding source dataset is hosted by ETH Zurich under DOI 10.3929/ethz-b-000559354. It contains three dimensional particle tracking velocimetry measurements for four flow configurations comprising a 3D printed aortic valve, two transcatheter aortic valve implantation configurations, and a severe stenosis condition. These four cases provide an independent experimental test of the spectral analysis across distinct valve geometries and flow states. For both datasets, the measured velocity field is projected onto a fixed streamwise path defined from the experimental geometry and phase averaged flow. The streamwise residual velocity is evaluated directly as a function of spatial position and cardiac phase. Its axial spatial spectrum is then calculated from the measured spatial coordinates. No temporal frequency to wavenumber conversion is used. The analysis quantifies the total wave energy, its instantaneous logarithmic growth or decay rate, and the ratio between high and low axial wavenumber energy. The resulting measurements show phase dependent redistribution of spectral energy toward higher axial wavenumbers. The response varies with anatomical region and valve condition. In the aneurysm model, the strongest redistribution is localized within the aneurysm dome and is substantially reduced by whole domain averaging. Across the aortic valve cases, spectral redistribution occurs over distinct portions of the pulsatile cycle and differs among the four configurations. The energetic analysis identifies intervals in which total wave energy decreases while the relative high wavenumber contribution increases. This observation provides the experimental benchmark for the central spectral prediction of the published theory and establishes that spectral redistribution and total wave energy growth are dynamically separable quantities in measured arterial flow fields. The experimental scope addresses the directly observable spatial spectral signature predicted by the theory. The present datasets do not provide a controlled Womersley number sweep, so the Womersley dependent resonant response identified in the theoretical study remains a subject for dedicated experiments. The deposited archive contains the complete analysis notebook, the final figure reconstruction notebook, derived numerical products, spectral diagnostics, bootstrap results, quality control records, processing provenance, figure source data, final publication figures, and software environment specifications. The original third party experimental datasets are not redistributed. Their published papers and hosted source records are identified through the related works associated with this Zenodo deposit so that the complete analysis can be reconstructed from the original measurements.

title: Aortic valve replacement in a patient with neurofibromatosis type 1: surgical considerations and perioperative management
authors: Tanushree Kar; Ashwani Bansal; Ankit Singhal
abstract: Abstract Introduction Cardiovascular involvement has been described in patients with neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF1), including congenital cardiac abnormalities, hypertension, and vascular lesions; however, clinically significant valvular disease requiring cardiac surgery is rarely reported. We report a case of severe aortic regurgitation (AR) in a patient with NF1 and highlight the perioperative evaluation, surgical decision-making, and management considerations relevant to cardiac surgery in this multisystem disorder. A 67-year-old female with NF1 presented with progressive dyspnea and was diagnosed with severe aortic regurgitation. Following comprehensive cardiovascular and perioperative evaluation, she successfully underwent bioprosthetic aortic valve replacement (AVR) with an uneventful recovery. Severe aortic regurgitation in patients with NF1 should be evaluated and managed according to established guidelines for valvular heart disease. Given the possibility of multisystem involvement, a thorough perioperative evaluation of patients with NF1 undergoing cardiac surgery remains paramount. A multidisciplinary and individually tailored approach is important, given the diverse systemic manifestations. Clinical trial number Not applicable.

title: Self-Expanding Stent-Assisted Reconstruction of Distal Supra-Aortic Vessels in Acute Type A Aortic Dissection: A Comparative Analysis
authors: Bowen Li; Feng Shi; Zhipeng Hu; Zongli Ren; zhiyong wu; Luocheng Li; Zhiwei Wang
abstract: Background: Supra-aortic vessel reconstruction during total aortic arch replacement in acute Stanford type A aortic dissection patients with dissected distal supra-aortic vessels remains technically challenging; proximal supra-aortic vessel replacement alone carries a high risk of neurological complications secondary to intimal inversion. This study aims to evaluate clinical outcomes of self-expanding stent-assisted supra-aortic vessel reconstruction compared with proximal replacement of supra-aortic vessels alone. Methods and Results: We performed a single-center retrospective comparative analysis of 49 consecutive patients undergoing emergency total aortic arch replacement for acute Stanford type A aortic dissection from January 2022 to December 2023. Patients were divided into two groups according to intraoperative anatomy and surgeon decision: self-expanding stent-assisted supra-aortic vessel reconstruction (SAVR, n = 26) and proximal replacement of supra-aortic vessels alone (PRVA, n = 23). Neurological outcomes related to supra-aortic vessel intimal inversion, operative parameters, blood product transfusion, and short-term complications were analyzed. The mean follow-up was 18.2 ± 4.1 months (range, 12–24 months). The SAVR group exhibited significantly lower supra-aortic vessel stenosis rate (3.8% vs. 30.4%, p < 0.001) and zero cases of intimal inversion-related luminal collapse versus five cases in the PRVA group (0 vs. 5, p = 0.02). Numerically fewer cases of symptomatic stroke (0% vs. 8.7%, p = 0.09) and radiographic cerebral infarction (3.8% vs. 13.0%, p = 0.17) were observed in the SAVR group, though the differences did not achieve statistical significance. Red blood cell and fresh frozen plasma transfusion requirements, mechanical ventilation duration, and ICU stay length were significantly lower in the SAVR cohort. Cardiopulmonary bypass time and 30-day mortality were comparable between groups. Conclusions: Self-expanding stent-assisted supra-aortic vessel reconstruction represents a promising technical option during total arch replacement for acute Stanford type A aortic dissection with distal supra-aortic dissection, associated with superior branch vessel patency and favorable numerical trends in neurological and recovery-related endpoints, with a comparable early-term safety profile. Potential benefits require further validation in larger cohorts.

title: EFFECTIVENESS OF TOTAL ARTERIAL REVASCULARIZATION COMPARED TO SAPHENOUS VEIN GRAFT IN MULTIVESSEL CORONARY ARTERY BYPASS SURGERY : A SYSTEMATIC REVIEW OF RANDOMIZED CONTROLLED TRIALS AND PRIMARY STUDIES
authors: I GNA Bayu Wiradinatha; I Made Indra Prasetya
journal: The Indonesian Journal of General Medicine
abstract: Introduction: Coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) remains the preferred revascularisation strategy for complex multivessel coronary artery disease, yet the great saphenous vein graft (SVG) is still used in the vast majority of operations despite its progressive late attrition. Total arterial revascularization (TAR), the complete avoidance of SVG, has been proposed to eliminate vein-graft failure, but its superiority rests largely on observational data. This review synthesised contemporary (2021-2026) randomised and primary evidence comparing TAR, or arterial-for-venous conduit substitution, with SVG-containing CABG.1–3 Methods: The study strictly adhered to the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis (PRISMA) 2020 guidelines. Randomised controlled trials (RCTs), prospective and retrospective cohort, case-control and cross-sectional studies comparing TAR (or an arterial conduit replacing SVG) with SVG-containing CABG in multivessel disease were eligible. Results: Twenty-one reports (3 RCTs; 18 observational reports from 15 cohorts; 18 unique cohorts; approximately 73,700 patients from 14 countries) were included. In non-randomised cohorts, TAR was associated with lower long-term all-cause mortality (5 independent estimates; HR 0.87, 95% CI 0.76-0.99; p = 0.041; I² = 35.4%), but the association lost significance after HKSJ adjustment (95% CI 0.71-1.06) and the prediction interval crossed unity (0.61-1.24). Randomised comparisons of arterial versus venous conduits to the second target showed no mortality difference (HR 0.93, 0.62-1.40; I² = 75.2%), although RAPCO-SV demonstrated fewer 15-year major adverse cardiac events (HR 0.71, 0.52-0.98). Across all seven estimates the pooled HR was 0.89 (0.78-1.03). Within the Australian and New Zealand registry, the benefit was consistent in men (HR 0.86) and women (0.82), in patients aged 70 years or older (0.87) and younger (0.80), but not demonstrable when LVEF was below 30% (0.87, 0.67-1.13). Early outcomes favoured TAR in small cohorts (in-hospital death/MACCE RR 0.35, 0.15-0.80), with shorter ventilation, intensive care and hospital stay. No small-study effect was detected (Egger p = 0.91). Certainty of evidence was low to very low.8–13 Discussion: The survival signal favouring TAR is modest, driven predominantly by one large binational registry, susceptible to residual confounding and surgeon-selection bias, and is not confirmed by randomised conduit trials; conversely, no signal of harm emerged, and arterial strategies appeared safe with favourable perioperative profiles in experienced centres. Benefit appears most plausible in patients with long life expectancy and high-grade non-LAD target stenoses.2,14,15 Conclusion: Contemporary evidence supports TAR as a safe strategy associated with a modest long-term survival advantage in observational data, but high-certainty proof of superiority over SVG-containing CABG is lacking. Individualised conduit selection by an experienced heart team is recommended pending adequately powered RCTs such as the Total Arterial (TA) Trial.1,3

title: Exploring the application value of preoperative femoral artery and vein cannulation in redo cardiac surgery
authors: Yi Hui Yu; Xun Li Zhang; Lei Wang; Li Qiong Xiao; Fu Hua Huang; Zhen Hong Wang
abstract: BACKGROUND: To explore the clinical value of preoperative femoral vessel cannulation in redo cardiac surgery. METHODS: A retrospective analysis was performed on the clinical data of 106 patients who underwent redo cardiac surgery in our hospital from January 2022 to December 2024. According to the cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) cannulation technique adopted, the patients were divided into the Femoral Cannulation group (n = 79) and the Traditional Central Cannulation group (n = 37). Preoperative baseline data, intraoperative CPB-related parameters, blood product consumption, and the incidence of postoperative complications were recorded and compared between the two groups. RESULTS: There were no statistically significant differences in preoperative baseline data or intraoperative parameters between the two groups (all P > 0.05). Similarly, no significant statistical differences were found in postoperative mortality, extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) utilization rate, acute kidney injury (AKI) incidence, or cognitive dysfunction incidence between the two groups. However, compared with the Traditional Central Cannulation group, the Femoral Cannulation group had significantly lower intraoperative packed red blood cell (PRBC) transfusion volume and a significantly lower incidence of major cardiovascular injuries (all P < 0.05). CONCLUSION: In redo cardiac surgery, preoperative femoral vessel cannulation can significantly reduce the incidence of major cardiovascular injuries and the demand for intraoperative blood transfusion, which is worthy of promotion and application in clinical practice.

title: Challenging the guidelines: longitudinal trends in left ventricular diameter and function in severe aortic regurgitation
authors: Shmuel Schwartzenberg; Amit Berkowitz; Tsahi T. Lerman; Tamir Bental; Mordehay Vaturi; Yair Goldberg; Yaron Shapira
abstract: Background Guidelines recommend aortic valve replacement (AVR) in patients with severe aortic regurgitation (AR) based on progressive changes in left ventricular (LV) function or size. We aimed to reassess the clinical relevance of current guideline recommendations pertaining to traditional echocardiographic measurements in routine practice. Methods Retrospective analysis of patients with severe AR who underwent serial echocardiographic follow-up over at least 18 months. The composite outcome was symptom-driven AVR, acute heart failure hospitalization, or death. We used a joint modelling approach to handle within-subject correlation and censoring. Results The cohort consisted of 140 patients, with a median follow-up of 93 months (interquartile range 58–130). LV end-systolic (LVESD) and fractional shortening (FS) showed a small but statistically significant longitudinal trend, while LVEDD did not. In three separate joint models adjusted for age at onset and sex, higher LVESD and LVEDD and lower FS were each associated with increased risk of the composite event. Each 1 mm increase in LVESD and LVEDD was associated with a 6% in risk; each 1% decrease in FS corresponded to a 12% increase in risk. Only 8 (5.7%) of patients were predicted to exceed the guideline-recommended LVEDD threshold of 65 mm over 10 years. Age at onset was also a significant risk factor, with each decade increasing risk by 65% for each of the three parallel joint models. Conclusion LV parameters show modest changes over time, despite holding strong prognostic value in patients with severe AR. LVEDD, while associated with overall risk, does not predictably or significantly dilate over time in most patients. AVR decisions should be based on comprehensive clinical and volumetric assessment rather than waiting for simple linear progression to guideline cutoffs.

title: Inflammatory regulatory mechanisms and targeted therapy of antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibodies in atherosclerosis (Review)
authors: Jingjing Cui; Qi Cui; Jinying Dou; Xiaoyan Li; Wenlong Chang; Shi LanChun; 安黎云
abstract: Atherosclerosis is the core pathological basis of cardiocerebrovascular diseases, and inflammatory response runs through the course of its occurrence, progression, and adverse events.Antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibodies (ANCAs) are autoantibodies targeting the lysosomal components in the cytoplasm of neutrophils and monocytes, and their association with atherosclerosis and pathogenic effects have become a research hotspot in cardiovascular medicine.The present review systematically examined the core molecular mechanisms of ANCA-mediated atherosclerosis, focusing on analyzing the pro-atherogenic effects of ANCAs through the regulation of monocyte dysfunction, induction of the formation of neutrophil extracellular traps, and activation of the synergistic complement-platelet pathway, and clarified the subtype-specific pathogenic pathways mediated by myeloperoxidase-ANCAs and proteinase 3-ANCAs.The present review also summarized the clinical evidence linking ANCA positivity to the risk of atherosclerosis, plaque characteristics, and clinical outcomes and explores the precise intervention strategies for targeting ANCA-related pathways in atherosclerosis.Finally, it highlighted the limitations of current research and future directions to provide a theoretical reference and novel insights for the risk stratification of populations at high risk of atherosclerosis and the precise management of residual inflammatory risk.

title: Protein lactylation in atherosclerosis – Mechanisms and therapeutic potential: A narrative review
authors: Lijuan Zou; Yingquan Zhu; Yining Lan; Yiheng Cheng; Bing Han; Jinglian Chen; Chao Qin; Daobin Cheng
abstract: Protein lactylation, which links cellular metabolism to gene regulation and protein function, may influence atherosclerosis. This narrative review explores its cellular mechanisms and therapeutic potential. We searched PubMed from inception to September 30, 2026, for English-language studies and reviews. The synthesis differentiated lactylation from lactate signaling and distinguished direct evidence in atherosclerosis from findings in other disease models. Predominantly preclinical evidence suggests that both histone and non-histone lactylation are involved in endothelial inflammation, endothelial-to-mesenchymal transition, macrophage polarization and ferroptosis, and vascular smooth muscle cell senescence, phenotypic remodeling, and calcification. Depending on the cellular context, modification site, and downstream targets, lactylation can either promote vascular injury or support anti-inflammatory responses and plaque stabilization. Candidate interventions target lactate production, transport, and lactylation-related enzymes, but their effects often lack specificity for lactylation. Much of the therapeutic evidence originates from non-atherosclerotic models, and clinical validation is currently absent. Therefore, therapeutic development should consider cell type, disease stage, and modification site, with validation of causal mechanisms, selectivity, and safety in atherosclerosis models prior to clinical translation.

title: The three‐element Windkessel parameters have empirical relations that uniquely define the mechanoenergetics of cardiac muscle shortening
authors: I.M.C.W.B. Kohombakadawala; Toan Pham; Kenneth Tran; Andrew James Taberner; June‐Chiew Han
abstract: Abstract The three‐element Windkessel model of the systemic circulation comprises terms that represent the resistance of peripheral vessels ( R p ), compliance of the arteries ( C ) and characteristic impedance ( Z c ) of the aorta. It is widely used to represent the biophysics of the arterial system, and can be used to model the vascular load that can be experimentally presented to isolated hearts or muscles. Reported values of the three Windkessel parameters span several orders of magnitude. By collecting literature data across species, we found empirical relationships that are naturally preserved among the three Windkessel parameters. We applied these empirical relationships in our experiments when prescribing loads to isolated cardiac muscles, and compared the results with loading protocols that do not preserve these empirical relationships. Thus, in our loading protocols, R p was varied, whereas C and Z c were either held constant or varied according to their empirical relationship with R p . Muscles responded to the prescribed loads and generated force–length work‐loops that were unique to the various loading protocols. The differences in work‐loops were most evident during muscle shortening in terms of the force achieved to commence shortening, the dynamics of the force during shortening and the force reached at the completion of shortening. With these loading protocol‐specific shortening, muscles liberated distinct amounts of shortening heat and performed different amounts of work, resulting in different levels of mechanical efficiency. In conclusion, the three‐element Windkessel parameters have empirical relationships that uniquely define the load and mechanoenergetics of cardiac muscle shortening. image Key points The heart pumps blood into the aorta against the arterial load imposed by the systemic vasculature. The biophysical properties of the vasculature are characterised by resistance, compliance and impedance. By compiling literature data across multiple species, we identified a relation that is rather ‘universal’ linking resistance and compliance, and another linking resistance and impedance. We conducted experiments on isolated cardiac muscles subjected to contract against loads that either conformed to or departed from the relations. We found that when the loads conformed to the relations, the mechanics, kinetics and energetics of muscle contraction and shortening were distinct from those loads that deviated from the relations. These findings establish a fundamental link between arterial load and cardiac muscle mechanoenergetics, demonstrating that presenting isolated muscles with loading conditions that conform to the empirical relations is essential for understanding the physiological mechanics of cardiac contraction.

title: Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation Followed by Lung Cancer Resection in an Older Patient: A Case Report
authors: Leena Khan; Syed S Qadri
abstract: The individual incidences of lung cancer and cardiovascular disease in the elderly population mean that there is a strong likelihood of both occurring simultaneously.Common practice for severe aortic stenosis (AS) would be surgical aortic valve replacement (AVR), unless deemed high-risk for this surgical procedure.Age and lung cancer both increase a patient's surgical risk; hence, the less invasive transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) to manage valve disease ahead of lung resection for lung cancer is an acceptable alternative after assessing other factors such as procedural risk, comorbidities, and prognosis.We present the case of an 82-year-old female patient who underwent a TAVI seven months before lung resection for an incidental diagnosis of lung cancer with staging T1b N0 M0.Postoperatively, she was treated for atrial fibrillation and lung collapse, then discharged after resolution of these complications on the eighth day after surgery, and remained well at follow-up three months later.This case report explores a situation when this sequence of interventions was appropriate due to increased surgical risk in the elderly population.

title: Occurrence and Antenatal Detection of Congenital Heart Malformations: Data from a Tertiary Obstetric Centre in Western Romania
authors: Adrian Ciulpan; Adrian Lăcătuşu; Liviu Laurentiu Pop; Corina Paul; Daniela Iacob; Brenda-Cristiana Bernad; Maghet Edida; Lucian Șerbănescu; Andrada-Ioana Dumitru; Monica Simina Mihuţa; Elena Silvia Bernad
abstract: Introduction: Congenital heart defects (CHDs) are the most frequent group of major congenital anomalies and impose a disproportionate burden on neonatal services. Antenatal detection determines where and how an affected newborn is delivered, yet reported detection rates differ several-fold between European countries. We aimed to quantify the postnatal occurrence and the antenatal detection of CHDs in a tertiary obstetric center in Western Romania and to place both figures in a comparable international context. Material and Methods: Retrospective observational study of all 10,113 births registered at the “Pius Brînzeu” County Clinical Emergency Hospital, Timișoara, between 2018 and 2022. Newborns with at least one cardiac lesion recorded on indication-based postnatal echocardiography were identified from the hospital electronic record. Interatrial communications and ductal patency recorded at the neonatal-index examination were counted inclusively and are analyzed separately from structural defects. A defect was classified as antenatally detected when it had been reported at any prenatal ultrasound scan and was subsequently confirmed postnatally. Proportions are reported with Wilson score 95% confidence intervals (CIs), separately at the level of the newborn and at the level of the individual lesion. Results: A total of 541 newborns carried at least one recorded cardiac lesion, giving an occurrence of 5.35% of births (95% CI 4.93–5.81); 670 individual lesions were recorded, a mean of 1.24 per affected newborn. Interatrial communication (n = 319; 47.6% of lesions) and ductal patency (n = 90; 13.4%) accounted for 61.0% of lesions; among the 261 structural defects, ventricular-septal defect was the most frequent (n = 121; 46.4%). An antenatal diagnosis had been made in 151 of 541 newborns (27.9%; 95% CI 24.3–31.8). Detection was highest for lesions distorting the four-chamber view, hypoplastic left-heart syndrome 4/5, and ventricular septal defect 80/121 (66.1%; 95% CI 57.3–73.9), and lowest for lesions requiring outflow-tract or arch views, including pulmonary stenosis 3/27 (11.1%; 95% CI 3.9–28.1) and aortic stenosis 0/12. Restricting the count to structural defects gives 13.1 to 25.8 affected newborns per 1000 births, against a EUROCAT total prevalence of 8.0 per 1000. Conclusions: The occurrence recorded here reflects tertiary referral, indication-based echocardiography, and an inclusive case definition rather than a genuine population excess, and is not interchangeable with registry prevalence. The antenatal detection rate of 27.9% sits between European settings without organized screening and those performing two or three routine scans per pregnancy. The detection deficit is concentrated in lesions that require outflow-tract or arch views. Because the views obtained at each scan were not recorded and detection was not stratified by prenatal-care status, the contribution of examination protocol and of access to care is inferred rather than demonstrated; both are testable hypotheses for a prospective, protocolized study.
